title: How a Godly Man Builds Brotherhood on the Weeks He's Too Busy for It
caption:
A busy week is exactly when a man convinces himself isolation is reasonable.

Nobody decides to disappear from his brothers. He just lets the calendar decide for him. The recurring hangout gets skipped for "just this week." The check-in text waits until he has more time. Eight weeks later, nobody's heard what he's actually fighting.

Block the slot like a deadline. Send the text before you feel like it, two minutes, not a whole hangout. Show up for thirty minutes instead of cancelling the two hours. And before the week ends, tell one man the real thing, not the update.

"Let us not neglect meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing." (Hebrews 10:25)

Brotherhood isn't what survives your leftover time. It's what you make room for.
